notes:
Summary: Large gov/critical-infra contact center operator evaluating an air-gapped on-prem deployment. Primary goals: keep call-center agents online during national-scale spikes, automate first-line triage and summarization, and enable tool-calls into existing ticketing and escalation systems without exfiltration. POC completed in isolated lab (no internet) using snapshot models; initial results: 65% reduction in average handle time on scripted inquiries, 40% faster ticket summarization accuracy vs baseline. CTO quote: 'We can’t have unpredictable fallbacks — need strict model allow-listing and signed binaries.'

Key requirements (verbatim/notes):
- Offline installable artifacts (signed containers/OVAs) + air-gap install playbook.
- KMS/HSM integration for keys, ability to rotate without cloud connectivity.
- Full audit logging (per-token/operation) retained for 7 years; exportable to SIEM.
- SAML 2.0 SSO + SCIM provisioning; RBAC mapped to AD groups.
- Deterministic rollback and pinned model versions; canaries must run in isolated subnet.
- Hard SLO: p95 latency < 300ms for agent-assist paths, sustained throughput 800 reqs/min during spikes.
- Tool-calling: suite connectors to Remedy/JIRA, internal incident bus, and PBX (Avaya).

POC notes: lab used dedicated GPU rack (on-prem), offline weights were loaded from secured archive. Observed KV cache warm-up variability — SE recommends warm standby and prefetch on known peaks. Security team requested full SBOM + CVE scan at image build time. Procurement: prefers 3-year committed pricing or subscription with hardware amortization.

Shorthand CRM-style follow-ups: security deep-dive scheduled, procurement asked for capital vs opex scenarios, need final hardware spec and installation SLA.
